name: Kiwi
grown_as: Hardy kiwi (kiwiberry), William's is 'Issai', a compact self-fertile variety. It is not the shop kiwi fruit (Actinidia deliciosa, with big furry brown fruit), which the iNaturalist photos were searched under: hardy kiwi has small, smooth, green, grape-sized fruit eaten skin and all. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A deciduous twining climber with no tendrils, 3 to 4 m for 'Issai' (other varieties far more), trained on wires or a pergola. Smooth reddish-brown young stems twisting round their supports; older bark grey-brown.

leaf.outline: Broadly oval to almost round, 8 to 12 cm long
leaf.tip: Abruptly narrowed to a short sharp point
leaf.margin: Fine, sharp, bristle-tipped teeth all round
leaf.veins: A midrib and 6 to 8 pairs of curving side veins, pressed in
leaf.surface: Smooth and hairless, glossy dark green above; paler beneath with tufts of hair in the vein angles
leaf.colour: Glossy dark green on red stalks; yellow in autumn

flower.form: A rounded open cup, facing down
flower.petals: Five (sometimes four or six), free, round, thick
flower.centre: Many stamens with dark purple-black anthers, round a white ovary topped with a star of thread-like white styles
flower.carried: One to three together on short stalks from the leaf angles of the new shoots, hanging beneath the leaves

fruit: Small, smooth, hairless berries, oval, 2 to 3 cm, like large grapes; bright green, sometimes flushed red on the sunny side, with a dry tuft at the tip. Hanging in small clusters along the stems under the leaves. September to October.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants
winter: Bare, twisting, reddish-brown to grey stems wound round their supports, with small buds sunk in the leaf scars.

leaf: broad oval leaf with an abrupt short point
fine sharp bristle teeth all round
glossy surface on a red stalk
bloom: five round white petals in a downward-facing cup
a star of white styles in the middle
young: a twining stem wound round a support, no tendrils
broad glossy leaves on red stalks
dormant: stems twisted round wires or posts, no tendrils
flower: white cup flowers hanging under the leaves in ones to threes
broad glossy leaves on red stalks
crop: small smooth green grape-sized fruit hanging along the stems

look_alikes: Shop kiwi (Actinidia deliciosa) has large heart-shaped leaves, hairy stems and furry brown fruit. Actinidia kolomikta has smaller leaves splashed white and pink. Grapes climb by tendrils and have lobed leaves.
checked: Written 16 November 2026 by Claude from field-guide knowledge. The iNaturalist photos are of the wrong species (Actinidia deliciosa). ⚠️ CHECK
